steps.what: Read the actual traffic control permit conditions and approved street or utility project plan in {DOCS}.
inputs: Actual current permit and approved traffic-control plan

steps.what: Monitor the actual street or utility project, checking signs, barriers, access and traffic arrangements against the permit conditions and investigating discrepancies.
Write actual inspection findings, locations and supporting observations in the traffic inspection application {OTHER}, with native repeated permit/project fields.
inputs: Verified permit and project identifiers from s1

steps.what: Discuss actual discrepancies with the traffic engineer or site contact and clarify any immediate escalation through the established safety procedure.
inputs: Actual engineer or site contact response

steps.what: Save the actual findings in the same traffic inspection record {OTHER}.

tasks.design: Configure native repeated project and permit fields in the existing inspection application {OTHER}. The technician reads the actual permit, performs the site monitoring, writes the actual findings and discusses discrepancies; the form does not certify compliance or alter traffic control.
tasks.previous_blocker: The same project identifiers can be re-entered for successive inspection findings.
tasks.enabler_now: Native inspection forms can reuse verified permit and project identifiers.
tasks.still_hard: Actual arrangements and traffic behaviour may differ from the approved drawing.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise a physical discrepancy and determine when engineering attention is needed.

ambition.what: Keep field attention on actual traffic conditions.

tasks.altitude: A small record-entry reduction, with no change in monitoring authority.

reach.learn: State what was observed and which approved condition it differs from.

evidence.claim: Native form fields can reuse project identifiers while actual traffic inspection and findings remain human work.

assumptions: Boundary includes actual permit reading, field monitoring, separate findings entry and actual discrepancy discussion. No invented recurring report or automated enforcement action is added.

The permit owner provides permit id, project id, site and revision; the technician verifies them in s1 and produces all new findings in s2-s3. Missing or conflicting identifiers are entered and checked manually. No free machine-readable interpretation of permit conditions is assumed.

Conditional E1 estimates, not measurements. Only repeated identifiers in s3 change; actual findings retain their time. Native configuration is tested first. Routine saving remains 1% fully retained and ungated.
unknowns: Are repeated project fields currently entered by hand?
research_questions: Can the form reuse identifiers without carrying findings from another inspection or permit revision?

already_counted.description: Actual permit reading, site monitoring, findings and discrepancy discussion

incremental.description: Check permit identifier and revision reuse

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross 15*0.10 = 1.5 minus 0.5 upkeep gives 1. Conservative case: the permit id is already carried by the inspection record, so keep the existing form and retain all monitoring, actual findings and discussion time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Check the actual traffic-engineer timing instructions, observation point and stopwatch readiness before the study.
outputs: Ready timing setup and defined events

steps.what: Observe the actual stoplights or other delays and operate the stopwatch at the defined event boundaries.
inputs: Actual signal phases and traffic delays

steps.what: Record each actual stopwatch timing with location, event definition, observation time and unusual conditions on the field timing sheet.
Check the timing sheet for the correct phase or delay definition, units and interrupted observations, marking invalid observations explicitly.
inputs: Actual raw timing sheet from s3
Actual field conditions and event definitions from s1-s2

steps.what: File the checked field timing sheet with its study records.

tasks.design: Retain actual stopwatch observation and its separate timing-sheet capture. Consider native stopwatch lap storage before building an app, but do not claim a saving unless it demonstrably replaces an existing transfer; controller logs also need to match the actual observed event before they can replace field measurement.
tasks.previous_blocker: Elapsed time depends on observing the correct physical event boundaries.
tasks.enabler_now: Digital lap storage exists, but availability alone does not remove this observation or its contextual record.
tasks.still_hard: Queue delay and the experienced signal phase are not necessarily the same as controller timestamps.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise the event being timed and note interruptions or atypical conditions.
tasks.altitude: No change in this stopwatch-based study.

reach.learn: Define repeatable events and distinguish actual observations from system timestamps.

build_days.consent_and_access: 0-0; no new system or data access

evidence.claim: Stopwatch observations require event identification and contextual capture; existing controller timestamps need not measure the same delay.

assumptions: Boundary includes the actual timing setup, observation, separate raw record write, validity check and filing. No record write is hidden in physical observation, and no duplicate transcription or report baseline is invented.
The technician produces actual timings in s2 and all location, event, timestamp and condition fields in s3. There is no assumed structured camera or signal-controller feed and no free extraction.

Conditional E1 shares for a direct stopwatch-and-sheet study. Native lap storage and a form are considered, but they do not remove new observational facts or shorten the time that passes. A measured existing transfer could support a different design; none is assumed here.
Incremental upkeep is zero because no tool, template or changed process is introduced. Ordinary sheet filing is fully retained and has no approval stage.
unknowns: Does the actual study already have an avoidable second entry?
Do any controller logs measure the same physical event?
research_questions: Compare event definitions and actual field conditions before considering controller logs or digital lap export as a substitute.

already_counted.description: All actual observation, separate timing capture, checks and filing

incremental.description: No changed process or new tool to maintain

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Actual timing and its separate record remain unchanged. Native lap storage does not by itself replace an evidenced manual transfer, and controller logs have not been shown to measure the same delay; no saving or upkeep is claimed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Field monitoring and actual event measurement remain human; small repeated permit fields may be reduced.
reach: Document actual transport observations for transportation inspectors
role.ambitious_version: Traffic studies whose records distinguish what was physically observed from what a controller reported.
